constraint.description: Matches on function and variable names

qualified-id.description: Exact, whole-string match on the method's fully-qualified id (no regex). On jvm/dex this is the method id, e.g. 'Lcom/example/Foo;->bar(I)V'; on pcode it is the namespace-qualified but address-free name, e.g. 'Foo::bar' or '<EXTERNAL>::system'; on lua it is the module-qualified IR name, e.g. 'lib.reader.read' or 'kong.pdk.request.get_headers' (a global root names itself, so 'ngx.req.get_headers').

qualified-ids.description: As 'qualified-id', but matches any id in the list.

constraint.description: Match on namespace parent of function/class
Matches a callsite by the function it occurs inside of (the caller)
Matches on whether function has code

value.description: Compares input integer to this value

constraint.description: Matches on any/all of the inner constraints
Describes things that should not match

port-spec.description: A propagation port: a positional selector (Argument(n), Argument(*), Return) followed by an optional access path. Each access-path segment is introduced by '.' and is either a decimal offset in brackets (.[8], .[-8]) or a field name. A field name that begins with '[' must be escaped so it is not read as an offset -- a Java array element is Argument(0).\[] -- and '.' or '\' inside a name is escaped the same way (.a\.b). The argument index is a non-negative decimal integer; the loader rejects a negative one.

source-sink-port-spec.description: A source/sink port. In addition to the positional selectors (Argument(n)/Argument(*)/Return), a source/sink may select a local by its source name with Variable(name), e.g. Variable(buf), optionally refined by a trailing access path (Variable(buf).headers). Variable(...) is valid only here, NOT on propagation inputs/outputs, and NOT with find: callsites. See port-spec for the access-path grammar.

field-spec.description: A bare access path, e.g. '', '.deref', '.[8].deref', '.\[_elem_]'. See port-spec for the grammar.

source-sink-model.description: Models associated SUT element as a source or a sink

kind.description: The taint label (your choice) to associate with the source/sink

port.description: The part of the matched SUT element to designate as source/sink. Positional (Argument(n)/Argument(*)/Return) or, for a local, by source name via Variable(name) (e.g. Variable(buf)).

field.description: The field of the matched variable to designate as source/sink

fields.description: The fields of the matched variable to designate as source/sink

all_fields.description: If true, sensitizes the port to all detected fields by name. Any fields referred to in the port itself are ignored. This feature will likely be removed in favor of simple star matching in future.

wildcard.description: Sink-only (rejected on sources/propagations). If true (the DEFAULT for sinks), the sink port matches any access-path extension of the port -- i.e. any concrete path having the port path as a prefix. E.g. port Argument(1) matches Argument(1).deref and Argument(1).[12].deref. Set false to match only the exact port path.

saturating.description: Source-only (rejected on sinks/propagations). If true (default false), marks a saturating source: the seeded vertex is tainted AND any subfield/offset read off it is tainted too, recursively, so the whole access-path subtree beneath the port is tainted. Use for values that are wholly attacker-controlled regardless of how callers index in, e.g. C's argv.

propagation-model.description: Models a method with a propagation

report-severity.description: How loudly to report a condition. Defaults to 'warn' everywhere it appears: a bridge that fires on nothing produces an analysis with fewer flows rather than an error, which is indistinguishable from a clean app, so the default has to say something.

artifact-language.description: An imported artifact's language, as `ctadl import -l` spells it.

program-scope.description: Which imports a generator applies to. Keys within one block are ANDed; an absent key leaves that dimension unconstrained. Distinct from how built-in default model files are selected (by virtual method table): the VMT cannot tell dex from apk from jar, and this can.

language.description: Exactly the one-element case of 'languages'. Giving both keys in one block is an error rather than a union -- a reader cannot tell which was meant.

languages.description: Admits a program whose language is any one of these. Not sugar: a language BOUNDARY has a set on each side, not a language -- 'the Java side' is jvm/jar/dex/apk and 'the native side' is pcode and eventually c. An empty list is an error, since it would match nothing quietly.

import.description: The import's name, as given to `ctadl import`.

port-map.description: One argument correspondence across a bridge: read it as 'the caller's from vertex IS the callee's to vertex'. Ports name SLOTS, not declaration order, so a hand-written map is correct only for the frontend the method was observed through (dex numbers parameters by register, so long/double consume two; jvm numbers them by argument position).

from.description: The caller-side port. Argument(*) is rejected: a wildcard has no correspondent on the other side.

to.description: The callee-side port, as the callee sees the parameter. May name a sub-path, e.g. 'Argument(0).stack.[1]'.

direction.description: Which way taint crosses. Defaults to 'both', matching how the engine treats an ordinary call.

bridge-model.description: Connects a callee matched in one program to its implementation in another, with an explicit argument correspondence. Index-time only: a bridge creates call facts, which the index fixpoint consumes, so `ctadl query --models` cannot act on one.

to.description: Side B, the implementation side. A match block, not a scope: side A stays in the generator's own find/where, so every existing matching feature applies to it verbatim.

where.description: Constraints selecting the implementation, in the same language everything else uses.

on-unmatched.description: What to do when side B matches nothing anywhere in the project. Independent of the generator-level 'on-unmatched', which covers side A. Set 'ignore' for a bridge written against a family of optional symbols. Not reported at all when side A matched nothing.

arguments.description: The port map. Omitted entirely means the identity mapping over the arity the two sides share, plus Return. The globals pseudo-parameter is ALWAYS mapped and is not user-visible; without it heap flows do not cross the boundary at all. Return means the normal return; a Java side's exception return is never mapped.

on-ambiguous.description: What to do when the pairing is not singleton x singleton. Every matched A pairs with every matched B (the full cross product); this reports that rather than restricting it.

find.description: The SUT element to match on

in.description: Scopes this generator to some of the project's imports. Omit to apply it to every one.

on-unmatched.description: Bridging models only: what to do when side A (this generator's own where) matches nothing anywhere in the project. The 'to' block carries the setting for side B.

model.description: How to model the matched SUT element

access_paths.description: Access paths that occur nowhere in the IR, declared by hand so the indexer registers them. The escape hatch for composition across a bridge: a pathful bridge composes with its callee's derived summary only where the summary's endpoints land exactly on the port's to-path, and flows needing deeper residues nobody declared are dropped, silently. Each entry uses the same grammar as a port's trailing path, e.g. '.next.next.next'.

forward_self.description: A forward_self model forwards calls to the matched methods to another method of self, possibly with a different signature. This is used, e.g., to forward ASyncTask.execute to doInBackground on the same object. Only makes sense for object oriented languages, e.g., Java.
